title: ERC4626YieldStrategy._acquireShares NatSpec says it 'credits the full nominal amount (no haircut)' but the code credits convertToAssets(sharesReceived) — a haircut
additionalLocations: ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:95 (@dev ... credits the full nominal amount (no haircut))
ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:115 (creditedPrincipal = vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived) — the actual, haircutting credit)
description: story-049 rewrote the credit logic in _acquireShares to credit convertToAssets(sharesReceived) (a value below the nominal amount whenever the vault has any entry-fee / share-rounding discrepancy — i.e. a haircut), but the function's NatSpec was NOT updated: line 93 still says the return is 'the full nominal `amount`' and line 95's @dev still says it 'credits the full nominal amount (no haircut)'. The docblock self-contradicts the very code change story-049 introduced (the inline comment at :112-115 even explains the haircut, three lines below the stale @dev). Pure documentation deviation — Law-2 faithfulness leg. The value/severity leg lives in ECON-A (L-16); this entry carries only the doc contradiction.
securityImpact: None directly. The realizable-NAV over-statement caused by the haircutting credit is the ECON-A value leg (L-16). This faithfulness entry covers the NatSpec contradiction only.
documentationCheck: DEVIATES. The NatSpec contradicts the implemented behaviour AND the inline comment within the same function.
recommendation: Update ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:93/95 NatSpec to state that _acquireShares credits the current exchange-rate value of the shares actually received (convertToAssets(sharesReceived)), NOT the full nominal amount — removing the 'no haircut' claim.
crossReferences: ECON-A / L-16 (value leg — fee-blind convertToAssets over-states redeemable NAV)
